headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Perplexity uploads user files and browsing context while Opik has broad network egress, but no shared filesystem or direct injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between Opik and Perplexity, so direct prompt injection is not provable. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of content from Opik outputs into Perplexity inputs, which is an unusual configuration and limits blast radius. Perplexity can browse and Opik can emit API-backed outputs, but neither profile shows automatic ingestion of the other’s output.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Opik-generated text into Perplexity prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is added between them, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted Opik output into Perplexity.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text.
Add a human review step before forwarding any Opik output.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity explicitly touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Opik has broad network egress. That creates a plausible path for sensitive content to leave the local environment if Opik outputs are forwarded into Perplexity or if Perplexity processes uploaded files containing secrets. The pair lacks a documented shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the default Perplexity upload/search behavior makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are uploaded to Perplexity, those contents enter vendor-hosted processing.
IF Opik outputs containing secrets are pasted into Perplexity, they may be retained in browsing context.
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or regulated data to Perplexity.
Redact sensitive fields before any upload or paste.
Use separate accounts for evaluation and research workflows.
Review Perplexity privacy settings before use.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to a local-only alternative.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Opik shows broad network egress, but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation; Perplexity is vendor-hosted and explicitly lacks host execution, filesystem write, and git modification. Overlapping mutable-resource conflict is therefore limited. The main overlap is network/API use, which is not a write conflict by itself.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free coordination, contention becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid granting filesystem write to Opik.
Do not expose shared git state to Perplexity.
Use explicit handoff files with one-writer ownership.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system that can render or act on retrieved content, and Opik can generate evaluation outputs that may be treated as authoritative if forwarded. Because no verification step between them is documented, Opik’s output could cascade into Perplexity’s answers or citations. Perplexity’s browsing reduces but does not eliminate this risk, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Opik output is pasted into Perplexity without verification, errors can propagate.
IF Perplexity is instructed to cite or summarize Opik-generated claims, it may amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Require source checking before forwarding Opik output.
Ask Perplexity to verify claims against primary sources.
Separate generation from publication workflows.
Flag any Opik-derived text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity documents vendor-hosted processing of uploaded documents and browsing context, while Opik is open-source and not shown handling regulated data. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced for Opik, so only Perplexity’s handling side is relevant. The risk is limited to compliance gaps if regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are uploaded to Perplexity without a DPA or approved transfer basis, compliance risk increases.
IF PHI is uploaded to Perplexity, a separate HIPAA review is required.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity.
Confirm contractual terms before using sensitive data.
Use anonymized or synthetic documents for testing.
Keep audit logs of uploads and deletions.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing controls.
